sampling_model.design: Observational covariance-fiber analysis with no interventions; the population complexity problem receives exact rational \(\Sigma\).
sampling_model.units: For the inference rung, \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) are independent centered Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\).
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is needed for orientation recovery. When vertices \(x\) and \(y\) are designated, the population total-effect fiber is exactly determined by restricted root-side feasibility: within one component its only possible values are zero and \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\), while conditional on structural feasibility the diagonal and cross-component fibers are the singleton sets containing one and zero, respectively.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population kernel uses exact Schur complements. The inference rung uses a simultaneous covariance region and performs no direct equality test on \(\widehat\Sigma\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The directed acyclic graph can be recovered from the joint Gaussian distribution under equal error variances.
Sources are identified by the smallest marginal variance, followed by conditional-variance source removal.
The variables are partitioned into blocks and each block shares the same error variance.
A generic distribution in a vertex-colored Gaussian DAG model is faithful to its DAG.
The minimum-label problems considered are W[2]-hard in the number of used labels.
Binary CSP on graph classes of unbounded treewidth has an ETH lower bound with a treewidth-over-log-treewidth exponent.
Set Cover has a base-two incidence-pathwidth barrier under the primal-pathwidth SETH.
An ASP reduction induces a polynomial-time bijection between the solution sets of the two instances.
An FPT-computable neighborhood function yields ordered Delay-FPT enumeration through a priority queue.
Split likelihood-ratio inversion gives finite-sample-valid total-effect confidence regions under equal variances.
Residual goodness-of-fit tests are inverted to construct confidence sets for causal orderings.

body.tldr: Arbitrary Gaussian error variances identify only a Markov-equivalence class, one common variance identifies the DAG, and a supplied partial-homoscedastic partition refines the class. This project studies the missing observational regime in which the equality partition is not supplied: a faithful rational Gaussian forest covariance is compatible with a root tuple when its exact regression residuals use at most \(K\) numerical values. The supplied-order dynamic program now has the refined binomial state bound \(\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\), preserving exact decision, uniqueness, and two-witness recovery and giving both the earlier base-two bound and a \(q_\pi^{O(K)}\) regime. The bounded-component algorithm costs \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\). For designated vertices, the population total-effect fiber is empty with the structural fiber; conditional on nonemptiness it is \(\{1\}\) on the diagonal, is \(\{0\}\) across components, and within a component is a subset of \(\{0,\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\}\). Each within-component value is present exactly when the corresponding side of the first path edge admits a feasible root, and both algorithms recover witnesses. The unrestricted \(K\)-frontier, uniqueness classification, and matching recurrence-width lower bound remain open. A covariance-region projection propagates sampling uncertainty to orientations and effects but is not claimed to be computationally efficient over the covariance region.

project_justification.gap: Published equal-variance and partial-homoscedastic theory either fixes one common level or supplies the equality partition. Generic minimum-label hardness does not survive the algebraic and arithmetic restrictions of Gaussian residual signatures.
project_justification.niche: The exact latent-\(K\) covariance fiber is a pointwise structural-identification object lying between fully identified equal-error models and unrestricted Markov equivalence, with a parameter whose algorithmic status is unknown.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a root-union reduction, an exact rational tree-signature realization theorem, symbolic root loci, positive algorithms at bounded component size and bounded recurrence width, and an exact tree-effect theorem. The supplied-order algorithm uses \(\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\) states per cut; the effect theorem reduces a within-component effect fiber to two root-side feasibility queries and recovers a witness for each attainable value. The unrestricted parameterized classification and matching lower bounds remain explicit open questions whose negative branch must certify edge residuals, positive definiteness, faithfulness, rationality, and bit length before using any Gaussian gadget.

body.related_work: Peters and Buehlmann (2014) establish full identification when all innovation variances are equal, the \(K=1\) endpoint. Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019) exploit the same common-variance ordering to build scalable recovery algorithms. Wu and Drton (2023) characterize Gaussian DAG equivalence when the variance partition is supplied and therefore motivate the latent-partition step without occupying it. Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus (2026) provide rational parameter recovery, algebraic Markov descriptions, and generic faithfulness for fixed vertex colorings; the inverse theorem here instead couples every alternative root of one covariance and certifies its piecewise diagonal and off-diagonal tree-product matrix by an arbitrary-root SEM calculation. Fellows, Guo, and Kanj (2010) show that several unrestricted minimum-label graph problems are W[2]-hard, but their label systems are not Gaussian-realizable. Marx (2010) and Lampis (2025) supply decomposition and fine-grained lower-bound techniques for CSP and Set Cover interfaces. Yato and Seta (2003) and Creignou et al. (2013) show why another-solution recovery needs solution-preserving reductions and a canonical neighborhood. Strieder and Drton (2023) and Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) motivate projecting structural uncertainty to total effects; here a forest-specific path calculation first identifies the population effect fiber as at most two values and the covariance-region proposition then supplies simultaneous coverage, without an efficient optimization claim for the projection over \(M\in\mathcal C_n\).
body.interpretation: The causal target remains the feasible orientation fiber rather than an observed regression coefficient. The tree-effect theorem proves their relationship: for distinct vertices in one component, a feasible root on the \(x\)-side of the first \(x\)--\(y\) path edge directs the entire path from \(x\) to \(y\), and its directed coefficient product telescopes to the observed covariance ratio \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\); a feasible root on the other side yields no directed path and effect zero. Faithfulness makes the ratio nonzero, so the two memberships are distinguished exactly. The refined-binomial-bound ordered dynamic program and the bounded-component search test both root-side restrictions and return witnesses. The confidence projection has a different role: it contains the resulting population effect fiber with the stated probability by ranging over covariances in \(\mathcal C_n\), but no efficient method for optimizing that range is asserted.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A common-center star encoding of Set Cover has a universal two-label center-root witness, while varying centers creates complementary residual labels. Moreover, every edge satisfies \(a_u b_{v\mid u}=a_v b_{u\mid v}\), and rational covariance requires a rational-square edge reconstruction. The first reduction test therefore enumerates one three-choice selector and one compatibility component, including all internal roots; any unintended witness or nonconstant auxiliary-label charge rejects that template. The existing twin-star family also rules out raw representative compression at empty width-one cuts, but it does not rule out a different symbolic FPT algorithm.
body.honest_scope: The root-union, root-locus, bounded-choice, refined-binomial-bound ordered-DP, piecewise rational-tree-realization, two-witness-transfer, \(K=1\), tree-effect-fiber, and projection-coverage results are proved in this note. The ordered dynamic program uses \(\sum_{i=0}^{\min(q_\pi,K)}\binom{q_\pi}{i}(K-i+1)\) states per cut and retains exact multiplicity and two witnesses. The tree-effect theorem proves that a within-component population effect fiber has at most the two values zero and \(\Sigma_{yx}/\Sigma_{xx}\), characterizes their presence by root-side feasibility, and recovers witnesses in both positive algorithmic regimes. The headline unrestricted \(K\)-classification, the arbitrary-algorithm \(q_\pi\) lower bound, and the unrestricted uniqueness transfer remain open-ended questions. Every hardness gadget must still verify the realization theorem's hypotheses and enumerate unintended roots and auxiliary labels. The confidence projection claims simultaneous coverage, not efficient optimization over \(M\in\mathcal C_n\), likelihood-ratio calibration, unknown-mean adjustment, or robustness to approximate equality.
